mainTopic: Acts forbidden on שבת and יום טוב (רשות, מצוה, שבות), the difference between יום טוב and שבת, and how belongings follow their owner's תחום
overview: The amud continues the משנה's list of acts that are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב. The גמרא explains why קידושין, חליצה and יבום can be called 'רשות' (optional). It says the 'רשות' acts are forbidden in case a person comes to write. It says הקדש, ערכין and חרמים are forbidden because they look like buying and selling. רב יוסף explains that separating תרומות is forbidden even when the portion is for a כהן that day. The גמרא adds that חלה may be taken from dough made on יום טוב. רבי יצחק then shows that all three lists are שבות, arranged in a 'לא מיבעיא' build-up. Next the גמרא sets our משנה against a משנה that allows lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב. רב יוסף's answer, which splits the two between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, is rejected by אביי. רב פפא's answer stands: our משנה follows בית שמאי and the skylight משנה follows בית הלל. Finally a new משנה teaches that animals and objects may go only where their owner may walk on יום טוב, and the גמרא begins to discuss it.

steps.title: Betrothal is optional when he already has a wife and children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the משנה calls קידושין optional because it is talking about a man who already has a wife and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he already has a wife and children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started just before this point. It explains why betrothing a woman can be listed as optional (רשות) and not as a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally marrying fulfills the מצוה of פריה ורביה. This man already has a wife and children, so he has already done that מצוה. Marrying another woman is therefore only optional.

keyTerms.meaning: a wife and children
optional; something you may do but are not commanded to do
the מצוה to have children

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a thought. The question it answers came just before this point: 'Isn't betrothing a woman a מצוה? Why is it called optional?'

phrases.english: because he has a wife and children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question about קידושין, which came before this point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Betrothal is always a מצוה, so it should not be listed as optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a man who already fulfilled פריה ורביה, so for him betrothal is optional.

steps.title: Aren't חליצה and יבום a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'no חליצה and no יבום' and asks why these are called optional, since they are a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We do not perform חליצה and we do not perform יבום.' But a person does a מצוה with these!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next items in the משנה's list of optional acts. It challenges the list, because חליצה and יבום are commands of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as the one about קידושין. The משנה put חליצה and יבום under 'רשות'. That seems wrong, since the תורה commands the brother to do one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: perform חליצה, the ceremony that releases the widow from יבום
perform יבום, marrying the widow of a brother who died without children
but look! (opens a challenge)
he is doing

phrases.english: We do not perform חליצה and we do not perform יבום.
But he is doing a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of challenge that was just answered about קידושין to the next items in the list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of חליצה and יבום under 'רשות'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doing an act the תורה commands cannot be called merely optional.

steps.title: When there is an older brother, the younger brother's יבום is optional
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a case where there is an older brother. The מצוה belongs first to the oldest brother, so if a younger brother does it, it counts as optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for the case where there is an older brother, and the מצוה of יבום belongs first to the oldest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows the משנה to a specific situation: a younger brother doing יבום or חליצה while an older brother is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The preferred way to do the מצוה is for the oldest brother to do it. So for a younger brother it is not his main obligation, and it falls under 'רשות'. The core מצוה of יבום still exists. Only this brother's part in it is optional.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for this case (the rule is talking about a specific case)
the older (oldest) brother
the main מצוה of יבום belongs to the oldest brother

steps.whatToRemember: חליצה and יבום are still a מצוה. They are listed as 'optional' only when a younger brother does them while an older brother is available.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where there is an older brother,
and the מצוה is for the oldest to perform יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יבום and חליצה are always a full מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: When an older brother is available, a younger brother's יבום or חליצה is treated as optional.

steps.title: What is the reason for all these prohibitions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why all the optional acts listed in the משנה are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of these, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for one reason that covers the whole list: judging, betrothing, חליצה and יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these acts is physical work. So it is not obvious why they should be forbidden on שבת. The גמרא wants to find the reason behind them.

keyTerms.meaning: all of them
what is the reason?

phrases.english: And all of them, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from asking why each act is called optional to asking why all of them are forbidden at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the optional acts are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: A decree in case someone writes
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן forbade these acts in case a person comes to write, which is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he will write.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. These acts usually involve writing a document, so the רבנן forbade the acts themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing is a real מלאכה. Judging, betrothing, חליצה and יבום are normally recorded in writing. To keep people far away from writing, the רבנן made a גזירה against doing the acts at all.

keyTerms.meaning: a decree made by the רבנן as a protective fence
in case he will write

steps.whatToRemember: All the 'רשות' acts are forbidden for one reason: a גזירה in case a person writes.

phrases.english: A decree, in case he will write.
phrases.notes: He means writing the document that goes with each act, such as a court ruling or a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The acts are forbidden because of a גזירה, in case a person comes to write.

steps.title: Consecrating, ערכין and חרמים are forbidden because they look like buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'מצוה' items: no הקדש, no ערכין and no חרמים. It explains that they are forbidden as a גזירה because they look like doing business.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the ones because of מצוה: we do not consecrate, we do not make valuation vows, and we do not make חרמים. It is a decree because of buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next group in the משנה. These are real מצוות, yet they are still forbidden. The גמרא gives the reason right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these acts moves ownership of property to the בית המקדש or to the כהנים. That looks like a business deal, and buying and selling is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב. So the רבנן made a גזירה against these acts too.

keyTerms.meaning: consecrate property to the בית המקדש (הקדש)
make a vow to give the set value (ערך) of a person
declare property חרם, given to the כהנים or to the בית המקדש
buying and selling; business

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reasons. The 'רשות' acts are forbidden in case a person writes. These 'מצוה' acts are forbidden because they look like buying and selling.
steps.whatToRemember: הקדש, ערכין and חרמים are real מצוות, but they are still forbidden on שבת and יום טוב because they resemble business.

phrases.english: And these are the ones because of מצוה:
We do not consecrate, and we do not make valuation vows,
and we do not declare property חרם.
It is a decree because of buying and selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'רשות' group and its reason to the 'מצוה' group and its different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrating, ערכין and חרמים are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב as a גזירה, because they resemble buying and selling.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to forbid separating תרומות and מעשרות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one may not separate תרומות and מעשרות on יום טוב, and challenges it as obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may not separate תרומות and מעשרות.' But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the משנה and asks why it even had to be said, because it seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומות and מעשרות turns food you are not allowed to eat into food you may eat. That is a kind of 'fixing,' which is clearly forbidden on יום טוב. So why would the משנה bother to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'lift up'; here it means separating (setting aside) the portions
The portions of produce given to a כהן
Tithes, the tenth portions taken from produce
'It is obvious!' A challenge that a teaching seems unnecessary

phrases.english: And one may not separate terumot and tithes.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the הקדש, ערכין and חרמים items to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to state that separating תרומות and מעשרות is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separating these portions makes the food usable, which is obviously forbidden, so the teaching seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Forbidden even if it will be given to a כהן that day
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the משנה teaches it is forbidden even when the portion will be given to a כהן on the same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: The משנה only needed to teach this for the case where one wants to give it to a כהן on that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by showing a case where we might have thought separating is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that since the כהן can use the תרומה right away on יום טוב, separating it counts as preparing food for יום טוב, which is allowed. The משנה tells us that even so, it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Taught.' Introduces a teaching from a ברייתא or a sage
'It was needed only for...' Introduces the special case that a teaching comes to cover
On that same day

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
It was needed only
to give it to a priest on that same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' challenge by naming a case where the rule is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the חידוש is a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separating for a כהן to use today might be allowed like any food preparation for יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when given to a כהן that same day, separating תרומות and מעשרות on יום טוב is forbidden.

steps.title: Dough made on יום טוב: חלה may be separated
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only to produce that was already טבל before יום טוב; dough made on יום טוב may have חלה separated and given to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule is only about produce that was already טבל from yesterday. But produce that became טבל today, like dough that needs חלה separated from it, we may separate it and give it to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule: it only covers produce that already needed separating before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the food was already טבל before יום טוב, the person could have separated it earlier, so he may not do it on יום טוב. Dough kneaded on יום טוב only became obligated in חלה today, so separating its חלה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And these words apply...' Introduces a limit on a rule
Produce from which the required portions have not yet been separated, so it may not be eaten
From yesterday, meaning from before יום טוב
The portion of dough given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This does not argue with רב יוסף. Produce that was טבל before יום טוב still may not be separated, even for a כהן today. Only produce that became טבל on יום טוב itself, like fresh dough, is allowed.

phrases.english: And these words apply
to produce that was untithed since yesterday,
but produce that became untithed now,
such as dough, to separate challah from it —
we separate it and give it to a priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from רב יוסף's answer to produce that was already טבל before יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce that was טבל before יום טוב may not be separated; dough that became obligated on יום טוב may have חלה separated and given to a כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical line: חלה from dough made on יום טוב may be separated on יום טוב.

steps.title: Are the רשות and מצוה items not שבות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording: by calling the later lists 'רשות' and 'מצוה', it seems to say they are not forbidden because of שבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are forbidden because of רשות, but not because of שבות? And these are forbidden because of מצוה, but not because of שבות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to how the משנה split its lists, and challenges that split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה called only the first list 'שבות.' That sounds as if the רשות items and the מצוה items are not שבות. But the גמרא already said they are all forbidden by the רבנן as a שבות, so the wording is confusing.

keyTerms.meaning: An act forbidden by the רבנן to keep שבת and יום טוב as days of rest
Something optional
'There is' / 'there is not'

phrases.english: And these, they are because of 'optional,'
but not because of shevut?
And these, they are because of 'מצוה,'
but not because of shevut?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי, מִשּׁוּם רְשׁוּת אִיכָּא, מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the overall structure of the משנה, which was discussed in steps 4 to 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's labels 'רשות' and 'מצוה' for its second and third lists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Labeling only the first list as שבות suggests the other lists are not שבות, but they are forbidden only as rabbinic שבות.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the משנה builds up step by step
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that all three lists are שבות. The משנה is using a 'לא מיבעיא' style, going from the obvious case to the more surprising one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The משנה is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that plain שבות is forbidden; even a שבות of something optional is forbidden. And there is no need to say that a שבות of something optional is forbidden; even a שבות of a מצוה is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers that every list in the משנה is שבות. The labels only show how the משנה builds from easy to surprising.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain שבות, with no מצוה at all, is obviously forbidden. The משנה then adds that even a שבות with a small מצוה side (רשות) is forbidden, and finally that even a שבות for a full מצוה is forbidden. The words 'רשות' and 'מצוה' describe each act, not a reason it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is no need to say...' A style that moves from the obvious case to a bigger חידוש
'He is saying.' Here, the משנה is speaking in this style
Plain, bare, with nothing extra
Also

steps.whatToRemember: All three lists in the משנה are forbidden as שבות. The order is a build-up: plain שבות, then שבות of רשות, then even שבות of מצוה are all forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even a מצוה does not override a rabbinic שבות on יום טוב in these cases.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
It is speaking in a 'there is no need to say' style:
There is no need to say that plain shevut is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ שְׁבוּת דִּרְשׁוּת נָמֵי אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but even shevut of an optional act is also forbidden.
And there is no need to say that shevut of an optional act is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ שְׁבוּת דְּמִצְוָה נָמֵי אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but even shevut of a מצוה is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, לָא מִבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the משנה's labels by rereading its structure.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the משנה ('לא מיבעיא' build-up)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The labels רשות and מצוה seemed to mean those lists are not שבות.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the lists are שבות; the labels show a build-up from plain שבות to שבות of רשות to שבות of מצוה, and all are forbidden.

steps.title: Contradiction from lowering produce through a skylight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's statement that all these things are forbidden even on יום טוב. It then contrasts it with another משנה that allows lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב but not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה said all these things are forbidden even on יום טוב, which means the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food. But another משנה says you may lower produce through a skylight on יום טוב and not on שבת. So there is another difference!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה and sets it against a different משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה suggests that the only thing allowed on יום טוב and not on שבת is food preparation. The skylight case is not food preparation. It is hard work done to save produce from being ruined. Yet that משנה allows it on יום טוב and not on שבת, so it looks like a second difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: two sources that seem to clash are set against each other
One may lower or drop down
A skylight or opening in the roof

phrases.english: All these, they said even regarding יום טוב,
And they raised a contradiction:
One may lower [produce] through a skylight on יום טוב,
but not on שבת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and opens a new contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that food preparation is the only difference between יום טוב and שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second משנה allows a non-food action, lowering produce to prevent loss, on יום טוב but not on שבת. That shows another difference.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the two משניות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that our משנה follows רבי אליעזר and the skylight משנה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not a problem. This משנה follows רבי אליעזר, and that one follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by saying the two משניות were taught according to two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not try to make the two sources agree. He says they come from a real מחלוקת. Our משנה, with no difference besides food, follows רבי אליעזר. The skylight משנה follows רבי יהושע. He proves this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; this introduces an answer
This one... that one; each word points to a different source

phrases.english: רב יוסף said: It is not difficult:
this one is רבי אליעזר,
phrases.notes: "This one" is our משנה, which lists no difference besides food.

phrases.english: that one is רבי יהושע.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the skylight משנה, which allows lowering produce on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split the sources between תנאים (הא רבי פלוני, הא רבי פלוני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות are one opinion, so they really clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each משנה follows a different תנא, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי אליעזר's view on an animal and its offspring in a pit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא about a mother animal and its offspring that fell into a pit on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר says you may lift out only the first one, to slaughter it. The second must be fed where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If an animal and its offspring fell into a pit, רבי אליעזר says you lift out the first in order to slaughter it, and you slaughter it. For the second, you feed it where it is so it will not die.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings his source, a ברייתא, and this step gives רבי אליעזר's half of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot slaughter both animals on the same day, so only one can be eaten on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר allows the hard work of lifting only for an animal you will actually eat. The second animal stays in the pit even though it could be lost. So, according to רב יוסף, he does not allow hard work on יום טוב just to prevent a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
An animal and its offspring, which may not be slaughtered on the same day
With the intention of; for the purpose of
Food or sustenance

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְבוֹר —
phrases.english: As it was taught: An animal and its offspring that fell into a pit —
phrases.notes: A mother animal and its child may not be slaughtered on the same day (ויקרא 22:28).

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ וְשׁוֹחֲטוֹ,
phrases.english: He lifts up the first in order to slaughter it, and he slaughters it,
and for the second, he gives it food in its place
so that it will not die.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְבוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רב יוסף's answer in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a מחלוקת תנאים about doing hard work on יום טוב to prevent a loss.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אותו ואת בנו that fell into a pit, here רבי אליעזר's opinion.

steps.title: The ברייתא continued: רבי יהושע allows lifting both with a trick
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says you lift out the first intending to slaughter it, then decide not to. You use a trick to lift the second, and afterward you may slaughter whichever one you want.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: You lift up the first in order to slaughter it, and then you don't slaughter it. Then you use a trick and lift up the second. If he wants, he slaughters this one; if he wants, he slaughters that one.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the ברייתא with רבי יהושע's opinion. He finds a way to get both animals out of the pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By changing his mind each time, the owner gets both animals out, even though only one will be eaten. רב יוסף reads this to mean רבי יהושע allows hard work on יום טוב to prevent a loss. That fits the skylight משנה. רבי אליעזר disagrees, and that fits our משנה, which allows nothing besides food.

keyTerms.meaning: Uses a trick or clever scheme
If he wants

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: our משנה, where food is the only difference, follows רבי אליעזר. The skylight משנה, which allows work to prevent loss on יום טוב, follows רבי יהושע. Both are drawn from the pit case of אותו ואת בנו.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע does not openly allow lifting an animal that will not be eaten. He gets there with a trick, lifting each one "in order to slaughter it." The leniency is that the trick works, not that the stated reason doesn't matter.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹחֲטוֹ,
phrases.english: He lifts up the first in order to slaughter it, and does not slaughter it,
and he goes back, uses a trick, and lifts up the second.
phrases.notes: The trick is that he says he now prefers to slaughter the second one, so he may lift it too.

phrases.english: If he wants, he slaughters this one;
if he wants, he slaughters that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 14 by giving the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע allows hard work on יום טוב to prevent a loss, matching the skylight משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אותו ואת בנו, here רבי יהושע's opinion.

steps.title: אביי: Maybe רבי אליעזר would allow saving the produce
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how he knows the pit case teaches us about the roof case. Maybe רבי אליעזר is strict only with the animal because it can be fed in the pit. Produce on a roof has no such option, so maybe there he would be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How do you know? Maybe רבי אליעזר was strict only there, because the animal can be fed where it is. But here, where there is no way to 'feed' the produce, he would not forbid it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer by showing that רבי אליעזר's ruling about the animals may not apply to the produce on the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that רבי אליעזר is strict about any hard work to prevent a loss on יום טוב. אביי points out a difference: the second animal will not be lost, because you can feed it in the pit. The produce on the roof has no such fix, so רבי אליעזר might allow moving it, and then he could not be the author of our strict משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
Perhaps; maybe
He only said this much (his ruling is limited to that case)
Feeding; providing food so the animal survives

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: From where do you know this?
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, who just brought the ברייתא about the animals in the pit.

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Eliezer only said his ruling there
because it is possible to feed the animal where it is,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר בְּפַרְנָסָה — לָא!
phrases.english: but here, where feeding is not possible, he would not forbid it!
phrases.notes: "Here" means the produce on the roof from the skylight משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רב יוסף drew from the ברייתא about the animals in the pit.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The link between רבי אליעזר's ruling in the pit case and the produce case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the pit case the loss can be avoided by feeding the animal; on the roof it cannot, so רבי אליעזר may be lenient there.

steps.title: אביי: Maybe רבי יהושע would forbid saving the produce
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second problem. Maybe רבי יהושע is lenient with the animals only because a trick is possible there. With the produce no trick is possible, so maybe he would forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another possibility: Maybe רבי יהושע was lenient only there, because it is possible to use a trick. But here, where a trick is not possible, he would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer from the other side, showing that רבי יהושע's leniency may not apply to the produce either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע allowed lifting the second animal only through a trick: you lift each one as if you plan to slaughter it. With produce on a roof there is no such trick, since it is obvious you are just saving your produce. So רבי יהושע might be strict there, and the ברייתא does not show he authored the lenient skylight משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or another way
To use a trick (a clever way around the problem)
There (the animals in the pit)
Here (the produce on the roof)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי shows the ברייתא proves nothing: רבי אליעזר may be lenient about produce, and רבי יהושע may be strict about it. So רב יוסף's answer loses its support.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם,
phrases.english: Alternatively: Rabbi Yehoshua only said his ruling there
because it is possible to use a trick.
phrases.notes: The trick from step 15: lift each animal as if you plan to slaughter it, then change your mind.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לְאַעֲרוֹמֵי — לָא.
phrases.english: But here, where a trick is not possible, he would not allow it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rejection of רב יוסף's proof, this time about רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The link between רבי יהושע's leniency in the pit case and the produce case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהושע's leniency depends on a trick, and no trick is possible with produce on a roof.

steps.title: רב פפא: One משנה follows בית שמאי, the other בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: Since רב יוסף's answer was pushed aside, רב פפא gives a new answer. Our strict משנה follows בית שמאי, and the lenient skylight משנה follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: It is not a problem. This one follows בית שמאי, and that one follows בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the contradiction from step 12 in a new way, matching each משנה to a different school.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא tells us we are dropping רב יוסף's answer. Our משנה, which treats יום טוב like שבת, fits בית שמאי. The skylight משנה, which allows on יום טוב what is forbidden on שבת, fits בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem
This one... that one
The school of Shammai
The school of Hillel

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said: It is not a problem:

phrases.aramaic: הָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, הָא בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: This one follows Beit Shammai, and that one follows Beit Hillel.
phrases.notes: Our strict משנה goes with בית שמאי; the lenient skylight משנה goes with בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's answer, which אביי just rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two משניות to two different schools (תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to follow one view, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows בית שמאי, who treat יום טוב like שבת here; the skylight משנה follows בית הלל, who are more lenient on יום טוב.

steps.title: Proof: בית הלל allow carrying out on יום טוב, בית שמאי forbid
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא supports his answer with a משנה. בית שמאי forbid carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public area on יום טוב, and בית הלל allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say: One may not carry out a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public domain. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show that בית שמאי and בית הלל really argue about how strict יום טוב is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these items are needed for cooking, and carrying them out is forbidden on שבת. בית שמאי forbid it on יום טוב too, treating it like שבת, while בית הלל allow it. This matches רב פפא's answer: בית שמאי would be strict about the produce on יום טוב, and בית הלל would be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Carry out (from a private area to a public one)
The public domain
Permit; allow

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer for now: our משנה follows בית שמאי, who are strict on יום טוב like on שבת. The skylight משנה follows בית הלל, who are lenient on יום טוב, just as they allow carrying these items out.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah: Beit Shammai say:
One may not carry out a child,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַלּוּלָב וְלֹא אֶת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: nor a lulav, nor a Torah scroll
into the public domain,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב פפא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי treat יום טוב like שבת in these cases, while בית הלל are lenient on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about carrying a child, a לולב, and a ספר תורה into the public domain on יום טוב.

steps.title: Maybe בית שמאי forbid only carrying out, not moving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רב פפא's proof may not work. בית שמאי may forbid only carrying into the public area, not moving produce around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that is not so. בית שמאי only said their strict rule there about carrying out to the public area. About simply moving things, they did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to knock down the proof רב פפא just brought from בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, בית שמאי forbid carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public area. Lowering produce from a roof is only moving it, not carrying it out. So maybe בית שמאי would allow it, and רב פפא's proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps that is not so
Carrying an object out from one area into another, such as into the public area
Moving an object around, even without taking it out
They only said their ruling up to this point (here, and not further)

phrases.english: Perhaps that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai only said their ruling there
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה from Step 19 about carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה.

phrases.english: about carrying out,
but about moving, they did not.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא לָא הִיא, עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof רב פפא brought in Step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from בית שמאי, not רב פפא's idea itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof is about carrying out (הוצאה), while the roof case is only about moving (טלטול)

steps.title: Moving is connected to carrying out, so the proof stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. Moving things is connected to carrying them out, so בית שמאי's strictness applies here too, and רב פפא's answer stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that moving things is not done for the sake of carrying them out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the challenge from Step 20 with a sharp question. This saves רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on moving things was made because moving can lead to carrying out. The two are linked, so בית שמאי, who are strict about carrying out on יום טוב, would also forbid moving the produce. That means our strict משנה, which treats יום טוב like שבת, can follow בית שמאי, while the lenient skylight משנה follows בית הלל, as רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a question showing the idea makes no sense)
For the sake of, connected to

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's answer stands. Our משנה, which says יום טוב is like שבת except for food, follows בית שמאי. The skylight משנה, which allows lowering produce on יום טוב, follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: Is that to say that moving
is not for the sake of carrying out?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ טִלְטוּל לָאו צוֹרֶךְ הוֹצָאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the rejection in Step 20
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly treats moving as unrelated to carrying out
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's answer stands: our strict משנה follows בית שמאי, and the lenient skylight משנה follows בית הלל.

steps.title: Animals and objects follow their owner's boundary
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that on יום טוב, animals and objects may go only where their owner may walk. This is true even if he handed his animal to his son or a shepherd.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Animals and objects are like the feet of their owner. If someone hands his animal to his son or to a shepherd, it is still like the feet of the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It teaches the basic rule that an animal or object is limited to where its owner is allowed to walk on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person has a walking limit on יום טוב (a תחום). His belongings share his limit. Even when someone else is looking after the animal, the owner's limit still decides where it can go.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (short for מתניתין)
Like the feet of the owner: it may go only where the owner may walk
One who hands over something to someone else's care
Shepherd

steps.confusionAlert: The animal follows the owner, not the person watching it. Even if the shepherd may walk farther, the animal may not.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Animals and objects
are like the feet of the owner.
phrases.notes: In other words, they may go only as far as the owner himself is allowed to walk on יום טוב.

phrases.english: One who hands over his animal
to his son or to the shepherd:
these are like the feet of the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal or object follows its owner's walking limit, even when it is handed to a son or shepherd.

steps.title: Objects owned together by brothers
steps.stepSummary: An object set aside for one brother follows that brother. An object not set aside for anyone may go only where all the brothers are allowed to go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Objects set aside for one of the brothers in the house are like his feet. Objects not set aside for anyone are like the place where all of them may go.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the rule to brothers who own objects together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an object belongs to just one brother's use, only his limit counts. If it is shared, every brother's limit counts. The object may go only to places that all of them are allowed to reach.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside for, designated for
Brothers
Like the place where they go: limited by all of their boundaries

phrases.english: Objects that are set aside
for one of the brothers in the house:
these are like his feet.
And those that are not set aside:
these are like the place where they go.
phrases.notes: In other words, the object may go only where every one of the brothers is allowed to walk.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּלִים הַמְיוּחָדִין לְאֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁבַּבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the basic rule to shared ownership
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A designated object follows its one owner. A shared object is limited by all the owners.

steps.title: A borrowed object: borrowed before or on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: An object borrowed before יום טוב follows the borrower. An object borrowed on יום טוב follows the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone borrows an object from his friend on ערב יום טוב, it is like the feet of the borrower. If he borrows it on יום טוב, it is like the feet of the lender.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains whose limit counts for a borrowed object. The answer depends on when it was borrowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides is who had the object when יום טוב began. If the borrower already had it, his limit counts. If it was still with the lender, the lender's limit stays with it all day.

keyTerms.meaning: The borrower
The lender
The day before יום טוב

phrases.english: One who borrows an object from his friend
on the day before the festival:
it is like the feet of the borrower.
If he borrows it on the festival:
it is like the feet of the lender.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another application of the basic rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever had the object when יום טוב began decides its limit.

steps.title: Dough made with a friend's ingredients
steps.stepSummary: A woman borrows spices, water, and salt from her friend for her dough. The dough is then limited by the boundaries of both women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, if a woman borrowed spices, water, and salt from her friend for her dough, the dough is like the feet of both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where one food item contains ingredients from two owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dough belongs to her, but some of its ingredients came from her friend. So both women's limits apply. The dough may go only where both of them may walk.

keyTerms.meaning: Spices
Dough
Like the feet of both of them

phrases.english: And similarly, a woman who borrowed from her friend
spices, water, and salt for her dough:
these are like the feet of both of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלָה מֵחֲבֶרְתָּהּ תַּבְלִין וּמַיִם וָמֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the borrowing case to mixed ingredients
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A food made with a friend's ingredients is limited by both owners' boundaries.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: water does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees about the water. It has no real substance in the dough, so it does not bring the friend's limit with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה exempts the case of water, because it has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with part of the last ruling, only regarding the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spices and salt stay noticeable in the food, so the friend's limit stays with them. Water blends in and is not felt as something real in the dough. So according to רבי יהודה, borrowed water does not tie the dough to the friend's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, does not apply the rule
Real substance

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of this משנה: an object goes only where its owner may walk. When two people own part of something, both limits apply. רבי יהודה holds that borrowed water does not count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda exempts the case of water,
because it has no substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 25 regarding water only
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, borrowed water does not bring the lender's limit into the dough.

steps.title: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא section begins and points back to the משנה we just learned, getting ready to say something about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה has ended and the גמרא is starting. This line is only a setup: the גמרא names "our משנה" because it is about to make a statement about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been ruled or challenged yet. The word מתניתין tells us the next statement will be about the משנה as a whole, meaning the rules about the boundaries of animals, objects, and the dough.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that comes after the משנה. Here it is written in short form as גְּמָ׳.
"Our משנה", the משנה we just learned.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full sentence. Don't look for a ruling here. The point the גמרא wants to make about the משנה comes right after.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Our mishna

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה (steps 22–26) into the גמרא's discussion of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is a setup line pointing to the משנה before the גמרא's statement about it.
